faqs.question: How long does the course take?
faqs.answer: Most undergraduate courses take 3-4 years of full-time study. Postgraduate taught courses typically take 1-2 years, while research degrees (PhD) can take 3-4 years.

faqs.question: How much are the tuition fees?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees vary by course and level of study. UK undergraduate fees are typically capped at £9,250 per year, while international and postgraduate fees can be higher.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements vary by course. Most undergraduate courses require A-levels or equivalent qualifications, typically AAA-BBB. Postgraduate courses usually require a 2:1 bachelor's degree.

faqs.question: Is the course available full-time or part-time?
faqs.answer: Many courses are available in both full-time and part-time formats. Full-time study is typically 3-4 years, while part-time study takes longer but offers flexibility.

faqs.question: Can I study this course online?
faqs.answer: Some courses are available as distance learning or online programmes. This allows students to study from anywhere with flexible scheduling.

faqs.question: What is the cost of student accommodation?
faqs.answer: Student accommodation costs vary by location and room type. Typically, university halls range from £100-£250 per week depending on the city and facilities.

faqs.question: What types of accommodation are available?
faqs.answer: Universities offer a range of accommodation options including en-suite rooms, shared bathrooms, studio flats, and family housing. On-campus halls are the most common for first-year students.

faqs.question: How far is the accommodation from campus?
faqs.answer: University accommodation is typically located on or near campus, usually within a 15-20 minute walk. Private housing may be further away but often cheaper.

faqs.question: When should I apply for accommodation?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to apply for accommodation as early as possible. Most universities open accommodation applications in spring for the following academic year.

faqs.question: What study modes are available for postgraduate courses?
faqs.answer: Postgraduate courses are typically available in full-time, part-time, and sometimes distance learning formats. Full-time MSc/MA programmes usually take 1 year.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available?
faqs.answer: Many universities offer scholarships, bursaries, and financial aid packages based on academic merit, background, or financial need. Check the university's funding page for details.

faqs.question: What is the difference between undergraduate and postgraduate study?
faqs.answer: Undergraduate study (e.g., bachelor's degrees) is the first level of higher education. Postgraduate study (master's, PhD) builds on a bachelor's degree and involves more specialised, advanced learning.

faqs.question: What subjects can I study?
faqs.answer: Universities offer courses across a wide range of subject areas including sciences, engineering, humanities, business, medicine, and the arts.

faqs.question: Are sandwich courses or placement years available?
faqs.answer: Some courses offer a sandwich year or work placement, typically taken between the second and final year. This provides valuable industry experience.

faqs.question: What English language tests are accepted and what scores do I need?
faqs.answer: Most universities accept IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic and Cambridge English. For postgraduate study a typical requirement is IELTS 6.0-6.5 overall with no band below 5.5-6.0, though requirements vary by course.

faqs.question: Are KCSE qualifications accepted for entry?
faqs.answer: Many UK universities accept KCSE for foundation or undergraduate entry, often with specific grade requirements. Check the university's country-specific page for Kenya for the exact KCSE grade equivalences.

faqs.question: Do international students need a student visa to study in the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes, most international students need a Student visa (formerly Tier 4). You will need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your university, proof of funds, and English language evidence.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to submit with my application?
faqs.answer: Applications typically require academic transcripts and certificates, English test results, a personal statement, reference letters, a copy of your passport, and proof of funding where applicable.

faqs.question: When should I apply and what are the deadlines?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to apply 6-12 months before your intended start date. Many postgraduate courses accept applications up to the start of term, but popular courses fill early and scholarship deadlines are often much earlier.

faqs.question: Can international students work while studying?
faqs.answer: On a Student visa you may usually work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during holidays, subject to your visa conditions.

faqs.question: How do international students pay tuition fees?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees can usually be paid in full or in instalments via bank transfer, international cards, or through approved agents. Some universities offer early-payment discounts.

faqs.question: What is the cost of living for international students in the UK?
faqs.answer: Living costs typically range from £1,000 to £1,500 per month depending on the city, covering accommodation, food, transport and personal expenses. London and the South East are generally more expensive.

faqs.question: Can I apply before I receive my final results or passport?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can apply with predicted grades or a conditional offer. A valid passport is needed for the visa application, but universities can issue a conditional offer before it is ready.

faqs.question: What happens if I have a study gap in my education?
faqs.answer: Universities may ask you to explain any study gap. Provide evidence of work, volunteering or other productive activity during the gap to strengthen your application.

faqs.question: Are there scholarships or bursaries for Kenyan international students?
faqs.answer: Many universities offer merit-based scholarships, country-specific awards and early-application discounts for international students. Check the university's funding and scholarship pages for eligibility and deadlines.

faqs.question: What KCSE English grade do I need for Aston University?
faqs.answer: For entry onto an undergraduate or postgraduate taught degree, a minimum Grade of C is acceptable from English Language in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE). For the MBChB medicine course, you need a minimum of Grade B in English.

faqs.question: I finished KCSE and want to do a foundation year - what do I need?
faqs.answer: For the International Foundation Year you need 12 years of study and an average of five subjects at grade C and above in KCSE, and the subjects must include the relevant subjects for your course.

faqs.question: What do I need to get onto a Masters at Aston from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a recognised Bachelor's honours second class (upper) degree. Aston can also consider a second class (lower) degree for some courses on a case-by-case basis if you have relevant industry experience.

faqs.question: I got a second class lower degree but I have work experience - can I still do a Masters?
faqs.answer: Yes, possibly. Aston can consider a Bachelor's honours second class (lower) degree for some courses on a case-by-case basis, especially if you have relevant industry experience.

faqs.question: Can I combine two scholarships at Aston?
faqs.answer: No. Aston scholarships cannot be combined - you are awarded the highest value scholarship available to you.

faqs.question: What study background do I need for undergraduate entry at Aston?
faqs.answer: You need 13 years of study, or 12 years plus a Diploma, a recognised Foundation programme, Cambridge A-Level, International Baccalaureate, BTech or HND.

faqs.question: How much is the postgraduate scholarship at BCU and who can get it?
faqs.answer: BCU is offering a scholarship of £3,000 to self-funding international postgraduate students joining on a full-time postgraduate taught Master's degree. It is applied as a tuition fee discount.

faqs.question: Is there an undergraduate scholarship at BCU?
faqs.answer: Yes, BCU is offering a scholarship of £5,000 to self-funding international undergraduate students.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS if I did KCSE English?
faqs.answer: BCU accepts the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) as evidence of English language. Check the individual scores required and the full list of accepted English qualifications on BCU's accepted qualifications and English tests page.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do most BCU courses require?
faqs.answer: Most courses require IELTS 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in each band, or equivalent, but some courses do have a higher requirement - check the individual course page.

faqs.question: I only have a KCSE certificate - can I apply for undergraduate entry at BCU?
faqs.answer: Yes, BCU accepts students who hold a KCSE certificate for undergraduate entry.

faqs.question: What class of degree do I need for a Masters at RGU from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a 4-year degree with a minimum of a second class lower classification with 50% or Grade C, or a Credit. A small number of postgraduate programmes do require a minimum of second class upper classification - refer to the relevant course page.

faqs.question: I got 50% in my degree - am I eligible for a Masters at RGU?
faqs.answer: Yes for most programmes. A 4-year degree with a minimum of a second class lower classification (50% or Grade C, or a Credit) meets the postgraduate requirement, although a small number of programmes need a second class upper instead.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do I need for postgraduate study at RGU?
faqs.answer: Postgraduate courses at RGU require IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in each area. Some courses require a higher score, so always check the course page.

faqs.question: I got a C in KCSE English - is that enough for RGU?
faqs.answer: For most courses, yes. RGU accepts KCSE English at grade C as the equivalent to an IELTS 6.5/6.0. Some courses have exceptions - check the English language requirements page.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do undergraduate courses at RGU need?
faqs.answer: Most undergraduate courses require an IELTS score of 6.0, with a minimum of 5.5 in each area.

faqs.question: What KCSE grades do I need for a foundation year at UCLan?
faqs.answer: For the foundation year you need Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) Grade B average in 5 or more subjects.

faqs.question: I have a Kenya Diploma - can I start in Year 1 at UCLan?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Kenya Diploma awarded by the Kenya National Examinations Council with a grade of 60% or above meets the Undergraduate (Year 1) entry requirement.

faqs.question: What do I need for a Masters at UCLan from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a minimum 2:2 in a bachelor degree from a recognised institution in a relevant subject.

faqs.question: What IELTS score does UCLan require?
faqs.answer: The standard English language entry requirement is IELTS 6.0 with no component score lower than 5.5, or equivalent.

faqs.question: My degree is a 2:2 but not in the same subject as the Masters I want - can I apply?
faqs.answer: The postgraduate requirement at UCLan is a minimum 2:2 in a bachelor degree from a recognised institution in a relevant subject, so the degree subject needs to be relevant to the course you want to study.

faqs.question: Which English language tests does Aston University accept for a Masters?
faqs.answer: We accept a wide range of English language qualifications including: IELTS Academic and IELTS Academic Online IELTS One Skill Retake TOEFL and TOEFL iBT (HOME edition is NOT accepted) Oxford ELLT (Global and Digital) Pearson Academic (PTE) Password Test (taken at NCUK centres only) Kaplan Test of English (KTE) Cambridge Advanced Test (CAE) Cambridge Proficiency Test (CPE) Duolingo Test.

faqs.question: How recent must my English test score be for Aston?
faqs.answer: Tests must be taken within the last 2 years from the start date of the course you are applying to study at Aston University.

faqs.question: Can I skip the English test if I studied in the UK?
faqs.answer: If you have studied for a minimum period of one year in the UK and achieved at least a 2:2 within the last five years then we will consider you to have met Aston's English language requirements for postgraduate study.

faqs.question: Does Aston accept KCSE English instead of IELTS?
faqs.answer: For entry onto an undergraduate or postgraduate taught degree, a minimum Grade of C is acceptable from English Language in Kenya Certificate for Secondary Education (KCSE).

faqs.question: What scholarships does Aston offer Kenyan students?
faqs.answer: We offer a range of scholarships for undergraduate and postgraduate study. Please see our international scholarships webpage for more information.

faqs.question: Can I combine an Aston scholarship with another award?
faqs.answer: Scholarships cannot be combined. Students are awarded the highest value scholarship available to them.

faqs.question: What postgraduate taught degrees does Aston University run?
faqs.answer: Aston offers specialist master's-level programmes such as Addiction and Mental Health MSc, and The Aston MBA is an intensive programme designed for professionals.

faqs.question: How long is a Masters at Aston University?
faqs.answer: Postgraduate MA/MSc courses at Aston, such as Addiction and Mental Health MSc, have a duration of one year.

faqs.question: How long is a PhD at Aston?
faqs.answer: Aston PhD research degrees have a duration of 3 years.

faqs.question: Where are Aston University courses based?
faqs.answer: Aston University courses are located in Birmingham.

faqs.question: Who can help me with my application to Aston from Kenya?
faqs.answer: Find out who to contact for help with your application, entry requirements for your country, and available scholarships.

faqs.question: Is there a Clearing route to study at Aston?
faqs.answer: Yes - Aston runs a Priority Clearing route: 'Clearing 2026: Join Priority Clearing'.

faqs.question: Where can I find Aston's tuition fees and funding options?
faqs.answer: For tuition fees, living costs and funding options, see Aston's Fees and Finance page (https://www.aston.ac.uk/current-students/fees-and-finance).

faqs.question: Where can I find accommodation information for Aston students?
faqs.answer: See Aston's Accommodation pages (https://www.aston.ac.uk/undergraduate/your-application/accommodation) for halls, costs and how to apply for student housing.

faqs.question: How can I contact Aston's Africa team about studying from Kenya?
faqs.answer: Contact Aston's Regional Manager for Africa, Babajide Ogundeji, by email at b.ogundeji@aston.ac.uk or africa@aston.ac.uk; phone and WhatsApp details are on the Aston Africa page.

faqs.question: Are there scholarships for Kenyan students at BCU?
faqs.answer: BCU's Kenya page includes a 'Scholarships' section for Kenyan applicants; see it for awards and eligibility.

faqs.question: What financial support does BCU offer Kenyan students?
faqs.answer: BCU's 'Study costs' section lists Fee costs and scholarships, Tuition fees, Living costs, Earn while you learn and How to pay, and the 'Financial support' section covers bursaries and funding.

faqs.question: Where can I find accommodation for studying at BCU?
faqs.answer: Find out everything you need to know about being a student at BCU, including accommodation, via the Accommodation section on BCU's Kenya page.

faqs.question: How do I apply to BCU from Kenya?
faqs.answer: Use the 'How to apply' section on BCU's Kenya page to apply to BCU as an international student.

faqs.question: What is BCU's application timeline for Kenyan students?
faqs.answer: BCU's Kenya page lists an 'Application timeline' section that covers each stage, from applying through to accepting an offer and planning your arrival.

faqs.question: How can I contact BCU about studying from Kenya?
faqs.answer: Use the 'Get in touch' / 'Contact us' section on BCU's Kenya page, or request a call from BCU's international team.

faqs.question: Can I speak to an education agent or advisor in Kenya for BCU?
faqs.answer: BCU's Kenya page lists Agents and Partnerships, plus an International Guide and 'Request a call' option to connect with BCU from Kenya.

faqs.question: Where can I find UCLan's English language requirements?
faqs.answer: See UCLan's 'English language entry requirements' page for accepted tests and band scores.

faqs.question: Where can I find scholarships for Kenyan students at the University of South Wales?
faqs.answer: The University of South Wales Kenya page has a 'FEES AND SCHOLARSHIPS' section; check 'Check your eligibility for scholarships, meet students from your country, and more.'

faqs.question: What scholarships and fees information does USW provide?
faqs.answer: USW's fees and scholarships page covers our affordable tuition fees and scholarship eligibility for international students.

faqs.question: Is accommodation available for Kenyan students at USW?
faqs.answer: USW provides an 'International Accommodation' section for finding student housing; see the International Accommodation page.

faqs.question: Where can I find visa and immigration information for USW?
faqs.answer: See USW's 'Visas and Pre Arrival' section (visas and arrival) for UK student visa guidance and pre-arrival information.

faqs.question: Do I need an English test for USW, or does my KCSE cover it?
faqs.answer: Check USW's 'English Language Programme(s)' section to see if your KCSE English meets the requirement or if you need an additional English test.

faqs.question: How do I apply to the University of South Wales?
faqs.answer: Use the 'How to Apply' section on USW's Kenya/international pages to start your application.

faqs.question: How do I contact the University of South Wales about studying in Kenya?
faqs.answer: Use the 'Contact' section on USW's International pages for Kenyan enquiries.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available to Kenyan students at Salford?
faqs.answer: Salford's Kenya page lists a 'Scholarships' section for Kenyan applicants; check it for awards and eligibility.

faqs.question: How do I find the cost of a course at Salford?
faqs.answer: Salford's Kenya page asks 'How much does a course cost?' - see Salford's fees pages for full tuition costs.

faqs.question: Who can I contact about studying at Salford from Kenya?
faqs.answer: Salford's Kenya page lists 'Contacts at the University of Salford', plus Scholarships and Education consultants sections, for Kenyan applicants.

faqs.question: How do I apply to the University of Hertfordshire as a Kenyan student?
faqs.answer: Applying to Hertfordshire is a quick and easy process: check the standard entry requirements for international students, submit your application, and follow the step-by-step guidance.

faqs.question: Will I get an applicant ID when I apply to Hertfordshire?
faqs.answer: Yes - you will receive your applicant ID as soon as you submit your application.

faqs.question: Where can I find step-by-step application advice for Hertfordshire?
faqs.answer: See Hertfordshire's 'Application guidance' for step-by-step advice on applying.

faqs.question: How much is Aston University accommodation per week?
faqs.answer: All campus accommodation is provided with Unite Students. Undergraduate ensuite rooms start at £172.20 per week, postgraduate ensuite at £130 per week, exchange students at £172.50 per week, and returning students' rooms from £160 per week.

faqs.question: Is there an upfront payment for Aston accommodation?
faqs.answer: Yes - an advance payment of £250 is required when you accept your Unite Students accommodation.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay rent before moving into Aston accommodation?
faqs.answer: Your first instalment must be paid before check-in; if you are waiting for a Student Maintenance Loan payment it can cover your first instalment.

faqs.question: Are there any discounts on Aston accommodation?
faqs.answer: Aston offers a 20% discount on all rooms from January 2026, with rooms available from January and April 2026 for new and existing students.

faqs.question: Can I cancel my Aston accommodation if my UK visa is refused?
faqs.answer: Under Aston's 'No Visa No Pay' policy, if you don't get your visa to come to your course you can cancel your Tenancy Agreement and have your deposit and advance rent refunded in full; this option is not available after 31 August before the tenancy starts.

faqs.question: When will I be invoiced for my Aston tuition fees?
faqs.answer: You will receive an invoice once you are formally enrolled, and you are set up to pay by instalments - 50% of your tuition fees by 31 October and 25% in Term 3 by online card instalments.

faqs.question: How do I pay my Aston tuition fees?
faqs.answer: Pay online via Aston's tuition payment service ('Pay now - Make an online tuition payment'), or apply for a Tuition Fee Loan through Student Finance England.

faqs.question: What happens if I pay my Aston tuition fees late?
faqs.answer: Late payment can incur tuition fee sanctions, for example the withdrawal of library and computer facilities; see the University Tuition Fee Policy for full details.

faqs.question: Does Aston offer bursaries, grants or tuition fee loans?
faqs.answer: Aston's Fees and Finance pages include a Grants, Bursaries and Scholarships section with information about tuition fee loans.

faqs.question: How much are my Aston tuition fees?
faqs.answer: The tuition fees are calculated by Academic Services, who can confirm the charge for your course; see your course offer letter and the Tuition Fee Policy for the exact amount.

faqs.question: What do my tuition fees cover at BCU?
faqs.answer: Your annual tuition fees cover everyday tuition, examination costs and membership of the Students' Union; they do not cover textbooks and other course materials.

faqs.question: How do I find the tuition fee for my BCU course?
faqs.answer: Search BCU's course pages and check the 'Fees and How to Apply' tab of the course you want to study; overseas students pay the higher 'overseas' tuition fee.

faqs.question: Does BCU offer undergraduate and postgraduate scholarships?
faqs.answer: Yes - BCU runs undergraduate and postgraduate scholarship schemes for international students.

faqs.question: Does a Kenyan student need a visa to study at USW in the UK?
faqs.answer: If you are an international student or a student from the European Economic Area and you do not hold EU Settled Status or EU Pre-Settled Status, you will need a visa to study in the UK.

faqs.question: Where can I find USW's step-by-step student visa guide?
faqs.answer: See USW's 'VISAS AND ARRIVAL: Our advice on making your visa application, arriving in the UK, and working whilst studying' — it includes a step-by-step guide to making a student visa application and credibility-interview preparation.

faqs.question: What are Hertfordshire's international application requirements?
faqs.answer: To apply to Hertfordshire you must meet our international entry requirements, submit your supporting documents and follow the step-by-step application guidance on the international apply pages.
